note: One entry per company. tiers must be ordered lowest pay to highest. All figures USD. ratio = CEO total / median employee as disclosed by the company. Add a company by copying an entry; the site reads this file on load.

companies.name: Apple
companies.caption: Apple's own filings put the median employee at $139,483 and the CEO at $74.3 million. Retail and engineering figures are employee self-reports; Apple does not publish them.

companies.name: Walmart
companies.caption: Walmart's median associate, by the company's own calculation, made $30,520. The CEO made $29,240,930. Walmart employs about 2.1 million people.

companies.name: Starbucks
companies.caption: Starbucks' median employee, by its own filing, is a part-time barista in the US who made $17,279. The CEO made $30,992,773. The prior year, with his sign-on stock grant counted, the gap was 6,666 to 1, the widest in the S&P 500.
companies.source: SEC DEF 14A, January 2026. Ratio computed from the two disclosed figures.

companies.name: Nike
companies.caption: Nike's median employee is a retail worker in the United Kingdom making $48,695. The CEO made $36,340,876.

companies.name: FTSE 100 (UK, index median)
companies.ratioNote: Median FTSE 100 CEO £4.4M vs UK median full-time worker £39,039
companies.caption: Not one company but the median across Britain's 100 largest. The typical FTSE 100 CEO earns the median UK full-time salary by lunchtime on the third working day of January.
companies.source: High Pay Centre, Fat Cat Day 2026. Converted at roughly 1.27 USD/GBP.

companies.name: PSEG (utility)
companies.caption: Included as a contrast. A large US utility with a unionized, skilled workforce: median employee $174,510, CEO $13.9 million. Same country, same rules, a tenth of the gap.
